name: NVIDIA BioNeMo Framework and ALCHEMI Toolkit-Ops
subcategory: GPU frameworks, recipes and accelerated checkpoints for biology (BioNeMo) and atomistic chemistry (ALCHEMI)
origin_detail: NVIDIA. BioNeMo is 'the development platform for AI-driven biology and drug discovery': open models, libraries, datasets and NIM microservices. ALCHEMI Toolkit-Ops offers GPU primitives for atomistic simulation.
flagship_projects: Accelerated checkpoints on Hugging Face (e.g. ESM-2 3B)

licences.data: uses public data (UniRef, OpenGenome2); NIM licensing not confirmed

openness_notes: BioNeMo Framework code is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE/license.txt, first committed 2024-08-07: 'Adding license, and contributing guidelines'). Checkpoints are 'available at huggingface.co/nvidia' under upstream terms; the ESM-2 3B conversion is MIT, trained on UniRef50/90. ALCHEMI Toolkit-Ops (neighbour lists, MD integrators, FIRE2/L-BFGS, DFT-D3 and Ewald/PME kernels in warp-lang with PyTorch and JAX bindings) is Apache-2.0. The fetched pages do not state the licensing of NIM microservices, and BioNeMo history before 2024 was not confirmed. Scored 2 (open framework tied to NVIDIA hardware and the proprietary CUDA stack, see C/nvidia.json, sold alongside NIM microservices); confidence low.

license_history.note: Licence file first committed 2024-08-07; earlier history not visible.

risk_events: Open code optimised for one vendor's GPUs; the commercial layer (NIM) is not documented on fetched pages
robustness: Apache-2.0 code can be forked, but performance depends on NVIDIA hardware and libraries.
physical_science_relevance: Accelerates training and inference of open biology models (ESM-2, Geneformer, AMPLIFY, Evo 2 recipes) and atomistic simulation kernels for MLIPs.

training_data.name: UniRef50/90 (ESM-2 checkpoints); OpenGenome2 (Llama recipe)
training_data.note: Framework hosts recipes and checkpoints for models trained on public data.

openness_effect_assessment: NVIDIA open-sources the software layer for physical-science AI to sell compute. The frameworks are permissive, but adoption is modest (under 1k stars) next to the academic models they accelerate.
key_takeaway: The hardware vendor's open science is complementary-goods strategy: Apache-2.0 frameworks and accelerated versions of other people's open models, with value captured in GPUs and enterprise services.
